youtube.title: Why the Ground Smells Before Rain 🌧️ #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
The smell of rain on dry ground is called petrichor, a word coined by two Australian scientists in 1964. Plants leak oils into soil during dry spells, and soil bacteria produce a compound called geosmin that humans can detect at tiny concentrations. When raindrops hit, they trap air bubbles that burst and release these compounds as airborne aerosols, as shown in a 2015 MIT study.
